record.content_text:
The mean of a set of data gives the average of the data. The mean is calculated by adding all the values together and dividing by the number of values in the data set.

For example, you have these results as your data: $\text{2; 6; 8; 10; 12; 14; 18}$.

The mean =

$$
\dfrac{\text{the sum of the data values}}{\text{the number of data values}} = \dfrac{\text{2 }\text{+ 6 }\text{+ 8 }\text{+ 10 }\text{+ 12 }\text{+ 14 }\text{+ 18 }}{ \text{7}} = \text{10}
$$

record_links.rationale: This worked example calculates the mean of a data set.

record.evidence_quote: Find the mean of the data set $\text{4; 6; 7; 3; 4; 8; 4; 2; 9}$.
record.prompt_text: Find the mean of the data set $\text{4; 6; 7; 3; 4; 8; 4; 2; 9}$.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Add the numbers.

Sum of the data values = $\text{4}$ + $\text{6}$ + $\text{7}$ + $\text{3}$ + $\text{4}$ + $\text{8}$ + $\text{4}$ + $\text{2}$ + $\text{9}$ = $\text{47}$.

Step 2: Count how many numbers there are in the data set.

Number of data values = 9.

Step 3: Find the mean by dividing the sum of the data values by the number of data values.

The mean =

$$
\dfrac{\text{the sum of the data values}}{\text{the number of data values}} = \dfrac{\text{47}}{\text{9}} = \text{5.2}
$$

The mean is 5.2.

heading_path.h3: Exercise 17.4: Find the mean of a data set

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 17.4: Find the mean of a data set 1. Consider the following set of data: $$ \text{8; 6; 9; 5; 11; 6; 7; 8} $$ Find the mean value of the data set. Round your answer to two decimal places.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 17.4: Find the mean of a data set

1. Consider the following set of data:

$$
\text{8; 6; 9; 5; 11; 6; 7; 8}
$$

Find the mean value of the data set. Round your answer to two decimal places.
record.answer_text:
Sum of the data values = $\text{8}$ + $\text{6}$ + $\text{9}$ + $\text{5}$ + $\text{11}$ + $\text{6}$ + $\text{7}$ + $\text{8}$ = $\text{60}$.

Number of data values = 8.

The mean =

$$
\dfrac{\text{the sum of the data values}}{\text{the number of data values}} = \dfrac{\text{60}}{\text{8}} = \text{7.5}
$$

The mean is 7.5.

record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 17.4: Find the mean of a data set

3. Find the mean value of the following data set. Round your answer to two decimal places.

\text{8; 7; 10; 8; 7; 6; 5; 5; 6; 11}
$$
record.answer_text:
Sum of the data values = $\text{8 + 7 + 10 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 5 + 6 + 11}$ = $\text{73}$.

Number of data values = 10.

Mean =

$$
\dfrac{\text{73}}{\text{10}} = \text{7.3}
$$

heading_path.h3: Worked example 17.9: Finding mean, median and mode for one data set

record.evidence_quote: Find the mean, median and mode for the data set $\text{5; 11; 9; 9; 10; 8; 9; 10; 6}$. - If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places. - If there are two or more modes, give all of the mode values, separated by "and" and/or a semi-colon (;).
record.prompt_text:
Find the mean, median and mode for the data set $\text{5; 11; 9; 9; 10; 8; 9; 10; 6}$.

- If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places.
- If there are two or more modes, give all of the mode values, separated by "and" and/or a semi-colon (;).
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Find the mean of the data set by adding up all the values in the data set and dividing by the number of data values.

$$
\text{The mean} = \dfrac{\text{the sum of the data values}}{\text{the number of data values}} = \dfrac{\text{5 + 11 + 9 + 9 + 10 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 6}}{\text{9}} = \dfrac{\text{77}}{\text{9}} = \text{8.56}
$$

Step 2: Find the mode by arranging the data in ascending order, and then finding the value or values that appear the most.

Arranging the data in order we get $\text{5; 6; 8; 9; 9; 9; 10; 10; 11}$.

The mode is 9 as it appears three times.

Step 3: Find the median by finding the middle value in the data set.

We have 9 values: $\text{5; 6; 8; 9; 9; 9; 10; 10; 11}$, so the median is the fifth value, which is a 9.

Answer: The mean is 8.56, the mode is 9, and the median is 9.

heading_path.h3: Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places. 1. Find the mean, median and mode for the following set of data: $\text{11; 7; 9; 5; 7; 8; 7}$.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set

If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places.

1. Find the mean, median and mode for the following set of data: $\text{11; 7; 9; 5; 7; 8; 7}$.
record.answer_text:
$$
\text{Mean} = \dfrac{\text{the sum of the data values}}{\text{the number of data values}} = \dfrac{\text{11 + 7 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8  + 7}}{\text{7}} = \dfrac{\text{54}}{\text{7}} = \text{7.71}
$$

Ascending order: $\text{5 ; 7 ; 7 ; 7 ; 8 ; 9 ; 11}$

7 is the mode as it appears three times.

The median (middle value) is 7.

Answer: The mean is 7.71, the mode is 7 and the median is 7.

heading_path.h3: Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places. 2. Find the mean, median and mode for the data set $\text{9; 6; 5; 9; 6; 10; 11; 8}$.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 17.7: Find the mean, median and mode of a data set

If necessary, round your answer to two decimal places.

2. Find the mean, median and mode for the data set $\text{9; 6; 5; 9; 6; 10; 11; 8}$.
record.answer_text:
$$
\text{Mean} = \dfrac{\text{9 + 6 + 5 + 9 + 6 + 10 + 11 + 8}}{\text{7}} = \dfrac{\text{64}}{\text{8}} = \text{8}
$$

Ascending order: $\text{5 ; 6 ; 6 ; 8 ; 9 ; 9 ; 10 ; 11}$

The modes are 6 and 9.

The median is $=\frac{\text{8} + \text{9}}{\text{2}} = \text{8.5}$.

Answer: The mean is 8, the modes are 6 and 9, and the median is 8.5.
